verses.zh: 耶稣离开那里，来到自己的家乡；门徒也跟从他。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] Jesus left that place and came to his hometown,[NOTE:2] and his disciples followed him.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.
Jesus’ hometown (where he spent his childhood years) was Nazareth, about 20 miles (30 km) southwest of Capernaum.

verses.zh: 到了安息日，他在会堂里教训人。众人听见，就甚希奇，说：「这人从哪里有这些事呢？所赐给他的是甚么智慧？他手所做的是何等的异能呢？
verses.en: When the Sabbath came, he began to teach in the synagogue.[NOTE:1] Many who heard him were astonished, saying, “Where did he get these ideas?[NOTE:2] And what is this wisdom that has been given to him? What are these miracles that are done through his hands?
notes: See the note on synagogue in 1:21. Jesus undoubtedly took the opportunity on this occasion to speak about his person and mission, and the relation of both to OT fulfillment.
Or “this teaching”; Grk “these things.” The response of the people centers upon the content of Jesus’ teaching, so the phrase “these ideas” was supplied in the text to make this clear.

verses.zh: 这不是那木匠吗？不是马利亚的儿子雅各、约西、犹大、西门的长兄吗？他妹妹们不也是在我们这里吗？」他们就厌弃他（厌弃他：原文是因他跌倒）。
verses.en: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son[NOTE:1] of Mary[NOTE:2] and brother of James, Joses, Judas, and Simon? And aren’t his sisters here with us?” And so they took offense at him.
notes: Evidently because of the possible offensiveness of designating Jesus a carpenter, several mss ([P45vid] ƒ13 33vid [565 579] 700 [2542] it vgmss) harmonize the words “carpenter, the son” to the parallel passage in Matt 13:55, “the son of the carpenter.” Almost all the rest of the mss read “the carpenter, the son.” Since the explicit designation of Jesus as a carpenter is the more difficult reading, and is much better attested, it is most likely correct.

The reference to Jesus as the carpenter is probably derogatory, indicating that they knew Jesus only as a common laborer like themselves. The reference to him as the son of Mary (even though Jesus’ father was probably dead by this point) appears to be somewhat derogatory, for a man was not regarded as his mother’s son in Jewish usage unless an insult was intended (cf. Judg 11:1-2; John 6:42; 8:41; 9:29).

verses.zh: 耶稣对他们说：「大凡先知，除了本地、亲属、本家之外，没有不被人尊敬的。」
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown, and among his relatives, and in his own house.”
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

verses.zh: 耶稣就在那里不得行甚么异能，不过按手在几个病人身上，治好他们。
verses.en: He was not able to do a miracle there, except to lay his hands on a few sick people and heal them.

verses.zh: 他也诧异他们不信，就往周围乡村教训人去了。
verses.en: And he was amazed because of their unbelief. Then[NOTE:1] he went around among the villages and taught.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

verses.zh: 耶稣叫了十二个门徒来，差遣他们两个两个地出去，也赐给他们权柄，制伏污鬼；
verses.en: Jesus[NOTE:1] called the twelve and began to send them out two by two. He gave them authority over the unclean spirits.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “He”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The phrase unclean spirits refers to evil spirits.

verses.zh: 并且嘱咐他们：「行路的时候不要带食物和口袋，腰袋里也不要带钱，除了拐杖以外，甚么都不要带；
verses.en: He instructed them to take nothing for the journey except a staff[NOTE:1]—no bread, no bag,[NOTE:2] no money in their belts—
notes: Neither Matt 10:9-10 nor Luke 9:3 allow for a staff. It might be that Matthew and Luke mean not taking an extra staff, or that the expression is merely rhetorical for “traveling light,” which has been rendered in two slightly different ways.
Or “no traveler’s bag”; or possibly “no beggar’s bag” (L&N 6.145; BDAG 811 s.v. πήρα).

verses.zh: 只要穿鞋，也不要穿两件褂子」；
verses.en: and to put on sandals but not to wear two tunics.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “shirts” (a long garment worn under the cloak next to the skin). The name for this garment (χιτών, chitōn) presents some difficulty in translation. Most modern readers would not understand what a “tunic” was any more than they would be familiar with a “chiton.” On the other hand, attempts to find a modern equivalent are also a problem: “Shirt” conveys the idea of a much shorter garment that covers only the upper body, and “undergarment” (given the styles of modern underwear) is more misleading still. “Tunic” was therefore employed, but with a note to explain its nature.

verses.zh: 又对他们说：「你们无论到何处，进了人的家，就住在那里，直到离开那地方。
verses.en: He said to them, “Wherever you enter a house, stay there[NOTE:1] until you leave the area.
notes: Jesus telling his disciples to stay there in one house contrasts with the practice of religious philosophers in the ancient world who went from house to house begging.

verses.zh: 何处的人不接待你们，不听你们，你们离开那里的时候，就把脚上的尘土跺下去，对他们作见证。」
verses.en: If a place will not welcome you or listen to you, as you go out from there, shake the dust off[NOTE:1] your feet as a testimony against them.”
notes: To shake the dust off represented shaking off the uncleanness from one’s feet; see Luke 10:11; Acts 13:51; 18:6. It was a sign of rejection.

verses.zh: 门徒就出去传道，叫人悔改，
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] they went out and preached that all should repent.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of previous action(s) in the narrative.

verses.zh: 又赶出许多的鬼，用油抹了许多病人，治好他们。
verses.en: They cast out many demons and anointed many sick people with olive oil and healed them.

verses.zh: 耶稣的名声传扬出来。希律王听见了，就说：「施洗的约翰从死里复活了，所以这些异能由他里面发出来。」
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] King Herod[NOTE:2] heard this, for Jesus’[NOTE:3] name had become known. Some[NOTE:4] were saying, “John the baptizer[NOTE:5] has been raised from the dead, and because of this, miraculous powers are at work in him.”
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.

Herod was technically not a king, but a tetrarch, a ruler with rank and authority lower than a king. A tetrarch ruled only with the approval of the Roman authorities. This was roughly equivalent to being governor of a region. In the NT, Herod, who ruled over Galilee, is called a king (Matt 14:9, Mark 6:14-29), reflecting popular usage rather than an official title.
Grk “his”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.

While Matthew and Luke consistently use the noun βαπτίστης (baptistēs, “the Baptist”) to refer to John, as a kind of a title, Mark prefers the substantival participle ὁ βαπτίζων (ho baptizōn, “the one who baptizes, the baptizer”) to describe him (only twice does he use the noun [Mark 6:25; 8:28]).

verses.zh: 但别人说：「是以利亚。」又有人说：「是先知，正像先知中的一位。」
verses.en: Others said, “He is Elijah.” Others said, “He is a prophet, like one of the prophets from the past.”

verses.zh: 希律听见却说：「是我所斩的约翰，他复活了。」
verses.en: But when Herod heard this, he said, “John, whom I beheaded, has been raised!”

verses.zh: 先是希律为他兄弟腓力的妻子希罗底的缘故，差人去拿住约翰，锁在监里，因为希律已经娶了那妇人。
verses.en: For Herod himself had sent men, arrested John, and bound him in prison on account of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, because Herod[NOTE:1] had married her.
notes: Grk “he”; here it is necessary to specify the referent as “Herod,” since the nearest previous antecedent in the translation is Philip.

verses.zh: 约翰曾对希律说：「你娶你兄弟的妻子是不合理的。」
verses.en: For John had repeatedly told[NOTE:1] Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The imperfect tense verb is here rendered with an iterative force.
It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife. This was a violation of OT law (Lev 18:16; 20:21). In addition, both Herod Antipas and Herodias had each left marriages to enter into this union.

verses.zh: 于是希罗底怀恨他，想要杀他，只是不能；
verses.en: So Herodias nursed a grudge against him and wanted to kill him. But[NOTE:1] she could not
notes: Grk “and.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.

verses.zh: 因为希律知道约翰是义人，是圣人，所以敬畏他，保护他，听他讲论，就多照着行（有古卷：游移不定），并且乐意听他。
verses.en: because Herod stood in awe of[NOTE:1] John and protected him, since he knew that John[NOTE:2] was a righteous and holy man. When Herod[NOTE:3] heard him, he was thoroughly baffled,[NOTE:4] and yet[NOTE:5] he liked to listen to John.[NOTE:6]
notes: Grk “was fearing,” “was respecting”; the imperfect tense connotes an ongoing fear or respect for John.
Grk “he”; the referent (John) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “he”; the referent (Herod) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Or “terribly disturbed,” “rather perplexed.” The verb ἀπορέω (aporeō) means “to be in perplexity, with the implication of serious anxiety” (L&N 32.9).tc In place of ἠπόρει (ēporei, “he was baffled”) the majority of mss (A C D ƒ1 33 M lat sy) have ἐποίει (epoiei, “he did”; cf. KJV’s “he did many things.”) The best mss (א B L [W] Θ co) support the reading followed in the translation. The variation may be no more than a simple case of confusion of letters, since the two readings look very much alike. The verb ποιέω (poieō, “I do”) certainly occurs more frequently than ἀπορέω (aporeō, “I am at a loss”), so a scribe would be more likely to write a more familiar word. Further, even though the reading ἐποίει is the harder reading in terms of the sense, it is virtually nonsensical here, rendering it most likely an unintentional scribal error.
Grk “and.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “and yet” to indicate the concessive nature of the final clause.
Grk “him”; the referent (John) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 有一天，恰巧是希律的生日，希律摆设筵席，请了大臣和千夫长，并加利利作首领的。
verses.en: But[NOTE:1] a suitable day[NOTE:2] came, when Herod gave a banquet on his birthday for his court officials, military commanders, and leaders of Galilee.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “but” to indicate the contrast present in this context.
Grk “a day of opportunity”; cf. BDAG 407 s.v. εὔκαιρος, “in our lit. only pert. to time than is considered a favorable occasion for some event or circumstance, well-timed, suitable.”

verses.zh: 希罗底的女儿进来跳舞，使希律和同席的人都欢喜。王就对女子说：「你随意向我求甚么，我必给你。」
verses.en: When his daughter Herodias[NOTE:1] came in and danced, she pleased Herod and his dinner guests. The king said to the girl, “Ask me for whatever you want and I will give it to you.”
notes: Behind “his daughter Herodias” is a most difficult textual problem. The reading adopted in the translation, τῆς θυγατρὸς αὐτοῦ ῾Ηρῳδιάδος (tēs thugatros autou herōdiados), is supported by א B D L Δ 565; it is also the most difficult reading internally since it describes Herodias as Herod’s daughter. Other readings are less awkward, but they do not have adequate external support. The reading τῆς θυγατρὸς αὐτῆς τῆς ῾Ηρῳδιάδος (tēs thugatros autēs tēs herōdiados, “the daughter of Herodias herself”) is supported by A C (W) Θ ƒ13 33 M, but this is also grammatically awkward. The easiest reading, τῆς θυγατρὸς τῆς ῾Ηρῳδιάδος (“the daughter of Herodias”) is supported by ƒ1, but this reading probably arose from an accidental omission of αὐτῆς in the previous reading. The reading τῆς θυγατρὸς αὐτοῦ ῾Ηρῳδιάδος, despite its historical difficulties, is most likely original due to external attestation and the fact that it most likely gave rise to the other readings as scribes sought to correct it.

verses.zh: 又对她起誓说：「随你向我求甚么，就是我国的一半，我也必给你。」
verses.en: He swore to her,[NOTE:1] “Whatever you ask I will give you, up to half my kingdom.”[NOTE:2]
notes: ‡ The witnesses here support several different readings: αὐτῇ πολλά (autē polla, “to her insistently”) is found in D Θ 565 700 it; πολλά is the reading of P45vid 28; both words are lacking in L; and א A B C2vid ƒ13 33 M lat have just αὐτῇ. The best candidates for authenticity, on external grounds, are αὐτῇ πολλά and αὐτῇ. So the issue revolves around whether πολλά is part of the text. On the one hand, πολλά used adverbially is a distinctive Markanism (10 of the 16 NT instances are found in Mark; of the other Gospels, Matthew alone adds a single example [Matt 9:14]). It could be argued that such an unremarkable term would go unnoticed by the scribes, and consequently would not have been inserted in imitation of Mark’s style observed elsewhere. On the other hand, the largest cluster of instances of an adverbial πολλά are in Mark 5-6, with the most recent example coming just three verses earlier (Mark 5:23, 38, 43; 6:20). Scribes may well have imitated the usage so recently and so frequently seen. Further, the best Alexandrian witnesses, as well as good representatives of the Western and Byzantines texts, lack πολλά. On the whole, though a decision is difficult, it is probably best to read the text without πολλά. NA28 places the word in brackets, indicating some doubt as to its authenticity.
The expression up to half my kingdom is a proverbial comment meaning “great wealth.”

verses.zh: 她就出去对她母亲说：「我可以求甚么呢？」她母亲说：「施洗约翰的头。」
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] she went out and said to her mother, “What should I ask for?” Her mother said,[NOTE:2] “The head of John the baptizer.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of previous action(s) in the narrative.
Grk “She said”; the referent (the girl’s mother) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

While Matthew and Luke consistently use the noun βαπτίστης (baptistēs, “the Baptist”) to refer to John, as a kind of a title, Mark employs the substantival participle ὁ βαπτίζων (ho baptizōn, “the one who baptizes, the baptizer”) to describe him (though twice he does use the noun [Mark 6:25; 8:28]).

verses.zh: 她就急忙进去见王，求他说：「我愿王立时把施洗约翰的头放在盘子里给我。」
verses.en: Immediately she hurried back to the king and made her request:[NOTE:1] “I want the head of John the Baptist on a platter immediately.”
notes: Grk “she asked, saying.” The participle λέγουσα (legousa) is redundant and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 王就甚忧愁；但因他所起的誓，又因同席的人，就不肯推辞，
verses.en: Although it grieved the king deeply,[NOTE:1] he did not want to reject her request because of his oath and his guests.
notes: Grk “and being deeply grieved, the king did not want.”

verses.zh: 随即差一个护卫兵，吩咐拿约翰的头来。护卫兵就去，在监里斩了约翰，
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] the king sent an executioner at once to bring John’s[NOTE:2] head, and he went and beheaded John in prison.
notes: Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of previous action(s) in the narrative.
Grk “his”; the referent (John the Baptist) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 把头放在盘子里，拿来给女子，女子就给她母亲。
verses.en: He brought his head on a platter and gave it to the girl, and the girl gave it to her mother.

verses.zh: 约翰的门徒听见了，就来把他的尸首领去，葬在坟墓里。
verses.en: When John’s[NOTE:1] disciples heard this, they came and took his body and placed it in a tomb.
notes: Grk “his”; the referent (John the Baptist) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 使徒聚集到耶稣那里，将一切所做的事、所传的道全告诉他。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] the apostles gathered around Jesus and told him everything they had done and taught.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

verses.zh: 他就说：「你们来，同我暗暗地到旷野地方去歇一歇。」这是因为来往的人多，他们连吃饭也没有工夫。
verses.en: He said to them, “Come with me privately to an isolated place and rest a while” (for many were coming and going, and there was no time to eat).

verses.zh: 他们就坐船，暗暗地往旷野地方去。
verses.en: So they went away by themselves in a boat[NOTE:1] to some remote place.
notes: See the note at Mark 1:19 for a description of the first-century fishing boat discovered in 1986 near Tiberias on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee.

verses.zh: 众人看见他们去，有许多认识他们的，就从各城步行，一同跑到那里，比他们先赶到了。
verses.en: But many saw them leaving and recognized them, and they hurried on foot[NOTE:1] from all the towns[NOTE:2] and arrived there ahead of them.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “ran together on foot.” The idea of συντρέχω (suntrechō) is “to come together quickly to form a crowd” (L&N 15.133).
Or “cities.”

The translation here follows the reading προῆλθον (proēlthon, “they preceded”), found in א B (0187) 892 lat co. Some mss (D 28 33 700) read συνῆλθον (sunēlthon, “arrived there with them”), while the majority of mss, most of them late (P84vid [A ƒ13] M syh), conflate the two readings (προῆλθον αὐτοὺς καὶ συνῆλθον πρὸς αὐτόν, “they preceded them and came together to him”). The reading adopted here thus has better external credentials than the variants. As well, it is the harder reading internally, being changed “by copyists who thought it unlikely that the crowd on the land could have outstripped the boat” (TCGNT 78).

verses.zh: 耶稣出来，见有许多的人，就怜悯他们，因为他们如同羊没有牧人一般，于是开口教训他们许多道理。
verses.en: As Jesus[NOTE:1] came ashore[NOTE:2] he saw the large crowd, and he had compassion on them because they were like sheep without a shepherd. So[NOTE:3] he taught them many things.
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Grk “came out [of the boat],” with the reference to the boat understood.
Grk “And.” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “So” to indicate this action is the result of Jesus’ compassion on the crowd in the narrative.

verses.zh: 天已经晚了，门徒进前来，说：「这是野地，天已经晚了，
verses.en: When it was already late, his disciples came to him and said, “This is an isolated place[NOTE:1] and it is already very late.
notes: Or “a desert” (meaning a deserted or desolate area with sparse vegetation).

verses.zh: 请叫众人散开，他们好往四面乡村里去，自己买甚么吃。」
verses.en: Send them away so that they can go into the surrounding countryside and villages and buy something for themselves to eat.”

verses.zh: 耶稣回答说：「你们给他们吃吧。」门徒说：「我们可以去买二十两银子的饼给他们吃吗？」
verses.en: But he answered them,[NOTE:1] “You[NOTE:2] give them something to eat.” And they said, “Should we go and buy bread for 200 silver coins[NOTE:3] and give it to them to eat?”
notes: Grk “answering, he said to them.” The participle ἀποκριθείς (apokritheis) is redundant, but the syntax of the sentence has been changed for clarity.
Here the pronoun ὑμεῖς (humeis) is used, making “you” in the translation emphatic.

The silver coin referred to here is the denarius. A denarius, inscribed with a picture of Tiberius Caesar, was worth approximately one day’s wage for a laborer. Two hundred denarii was thus approximately equal to eight months’ wages. The disciples did not have the resources in their possession to feed the large crowd, so Jesus’ request is his way of causing them to trust him as part of their growth in discipleship.

verses.zh: 耶稣说：「你们有多少饼，可以去看看。」他们知道了，就说：「五个饼，两条鱼。」
verses.en: He said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go and see.” When they found out, they said, “Five—and two fish.”

verses.zh: 耶稣吩咐他们，叫众人一帮一帮地坐在青草地上。
verses.en: Then he directed them all to sit down in groups on the green grass.

verses.zh: 众人就一排一排地坐下，有一百一排的，有五十一排的。
verses.en: So they reclined in groups of hundreds and fifties.

verses.zh: 耶稣拿着这五个饼，两条鱼，望着天祝福，擘开饼，递给门徒，摆在众人面前，也把那两条鱼分给众人。
verses.en: He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven, he gave thanks and broke the loaves. He[NOTE:1] gave them to his[NOTE:2] disciples to serve the people, and he divided the two fish among them all.
notes: Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.

Grk “the disciples”; the Greek article has been translated here as a possessive pronoun (ExSyn 215).tc ‡ Most mss (P45 A D W Θ ƒ1,13 M lat sy) have αὐτοῦ (autou, “his”) after τοῖς μαθηταῖς (tois mathētais, “the disciples”), but several excellent witnesses (א B L Δ 33 579 892 1241 1424) lack the pronoun. This kind of variant is often a predictable expansion of the text; further, that many significant mss lack the pronoun gives support for the shorter reading. For these reasons, the pronoun is considered to be secondary. NA28 puts αὐτοῦ in brackets, indicating some doubts as to its authenticity.

verses.zh: 他们都吃，并且吃饱了。
verses.en: They all ate and were satisfied,

verses.zh: 门徒就把碎饼碎鱼收拾起来，装满了十二个篮子。
verses.en: and they picked up the broken pieces and fish that were left over, 12 baskets full.

verses.zh: 吃饼的男人共有五千。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] there were 5,000 men[NOTE:2] who ate the bread.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate a somewhat parenthetical remark by the author.
The Greek word here is ἀνήρ, meaning “adult male” (BDAG 79 s.v. 1). According to Matt 14:21, Jesus fed not only 5,000 men, but also an unspecified number of women and children.

Many good mss (P45 א D W Θ ƒ1,13 28 565 700 2542 lat sa) lack τοὺς ἄρτους (tous artous, lit. “the loaves” [here translated “the bread”]). On the other hand, just as weighty mss (A B L 33 M) have the words. Although a decision is not easy, the most satisfactory explanation seems to be that scribes were more prone to delete than to add the words here. They may have been puzzled as to why “the bread” should be mentioned without a corresponding mention of “fish.” Since neither Matt 14:21 or Luke 9:17 explicitly mention the bread, a desire for harmonization may have motivated the copyists as well. On the other hand, D and W are prone to longer, explanatory readings. Since they both lack the words here, it is likely that their archetypes also lacked the words. But given Mark’s pleonastic style, the good witnesses with “the bread,” and a reasonable explanation for the omission, “the bread” is most likely part of the initial text of Mark.

verses.zh: 耶稣随即催门徒上船，先渡到那边伯赛大去，等他叫众人散开。
verses.en: Immediately Jesus[NOTE:1] made his disciples get into the boat[NOTE:2] and go on ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he dispersed the crowd.
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
See the note at Mark 1:19 for a description of the first-century fishing boat discovered in 1986 near Tiberias on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee.

verses.zh: 他既辞别了他们，就往山上去祷告。
verses.en: After saying goodbye to them, he went to the mountain to pray.

verses.zh: 到了晚上，船在海中，耶稣独自在岸上；
verses.en: When evening came, the boat was in the middle of the sea and he was alone on the land.

verses.zh: 看见门徒因风不顺，摇橹甚苦。夜里约有四更天，就在海面上走，往他们那里去，意思要走过他们去。
verses.en: He[NOTE:1] saw them straining at the oars because the wind was against them. As the night was ending,[NOTE:2] he came to them walking on the sea,[NOTE:3] for[NOTE:4] he wanted to pass by them.[NOTE:5]
notes: This verse is one complete sentence in the Greek text, but it has been broken into two sentences in English for clarity.
Grk “about the fourth watch of the night,” between 3 a.m. and 6 a.m.
Or “on the lake.”
The καί (kai) was translated so as to introduce a subordinate clause, i.e., with the use of “for.” See BDF §442.9.

The statement he wanted to pass by them is somewhat difficult to understand. There are at least two common interpretations: (1) it refers to the perspective of the disciples, that is, from their point of view it seemed that Jesus wanted to pass by them; or (2) it refers to a theophany and uses the language of the Greek Old Testament (LXX) when God “passed by” Moses at Sinai (cf. Exod 33:19, 22). According to the latter alternative, Jesus is “passing by” the disciples during their struggle, in order to assure them of his presence with them. See W L. Lane, Mark (NICNT), 236.

verses.zh: 但门徒看见他在海面上走，以为是鬼怪，就喊叫起来；
verses.en: When they saw him walking on the water[NOTE:1] they thought he was a ghost. They[NOTE:2] cried out,
notes: Grk “on the sea,” “on the lake.” The translation “water” has been used here for stylistic reasons (cf. the same phrase in v. 48).
Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.

verses.zh: 因为他们都看见了他，且甚惊慌。耶稣连忙对他们说：「你们放心！是我，不要怕！」
verses.en: for they all saw him and were terrified. But immediately he spoke to them:[NOTE:1] “Have courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
notes: Grk “he spoke with them, and said to them.”

verses.zh: 于是到他们那里，上了船，风就住了；他们心里十分惊奇。
verses.en: Then he went up with them into the boat, and the wind ceased. They were completely astonished,

verses.zh: 这是因为他们不明白那分饼的事，心里还是愚顽。
verses.en: because they did not understand about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.

verses.zh: 既渡过去，来到革尼撒勒地方，就靠了岸，
verses.en: After they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret[NOTE:1] and anchored there.
notes: Gennesaret was a fertile plain south of Capernaum (see also Matt 14:34). This name was also sometimes used for the Sea of Galilee (Luke 5:1).

verses.zh: 一下船，众人认得是耶稣，
verses.en: As they got out of the boat, people immediately recognized Jesus.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “him”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 就跑遍那一带地方，听见他在何处，便将有病的人用褥子抬到那里。
verses.en: They ran through that whole region and began to bring the sick on mats to wherever he was rumored to be.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “wherever they heard he was.”

verses.zh: 凡耶稣所到的地方，或村中，或城里，或乡间，他们都将病人放在街市上，求耶稣只容他们摸他的衣裳繸子；凡摸着的人就都好了。
verses.en: And wherever he would go—into villages, towns, or countryside—they would place the sick in the marketplaces,[NOTE:1] and would ask him if[NOTE:2] they could just touch the edge of his cloak, and all who touched it were healed.
notes: The marketplaces (Greek agora) were not only places of trade and commerce in the first century Greco-Roman world. They were places of discussion and dialogue (the “public square”), places of judgment (courts held session there), places for idle people and those seeking work, and places for children to play.
Grk “asked that they might touch.”
